This looks the same as candidate 2. The headline is strong and the order is right. The photo has a left gap but runs off the right edge, so it is out of line with the headline. The order is right (big headline, then the photo, then copy, then the contact block) and the headline clearly leads. There is a large dead gap between the photo and the descriptor copy. The top accent bar and the contact box hang off edges in a way that looks accidental.

The headline is too small for a tall canvas and sits loosely in a large empty area. Big empty gaps surround the photo. The descriptor line and the contact box are shrunk to tiny, barely readable text and pushed into the bottom corners. Overall it is badly underscaled.

The whole banner is just shrunk and dropped in the middle of the canvas, leaving about 60% of it as empty white bands above and below. The descriptor line and the contact text are too small to read, and nothing was rearranged for a tall format.

The original layout is copied unchanged and centred, leaving empty bands of about 110 px on the left and 130 px on the right. Nothing was rearranged for the wider canvas, and the headline is no bigger than in the original.

The photo is widened sensibly and the dots are spread out, but a 130 px dead gap separates the photo from the text block. The text sits close to the right edge, so the composition looks split rather than grouped.

The decorative dots render as a row of blurry grey cross smudges right next to the subhead, which is a visible artifact. The headline is jammed against the photo edge with no gutter, the photo touches the top edge, and the top-right corner is left empty.

The headline is gone entirely. The design is reduced to a cropped photo strip of the kitten's face and the dog's tongue with stray fragments of the coral and yellow shapes, so the message, brand shapes and hierarchy are all lost.

Same core failures as candidate 2: the headline is tiny and stacked in four lines in a 50 px strip, it loses the coral pill and sits directly on the cat's fur, so it is hard to read. The headline is squeezed into tiny four-line white text pinned to the left edge. Best of the three: the LUST/FOR/WIN lockup is scaled to the full 160 px width, so it stays readable and is clearly the focal point. The photo crop is mostly black hand wrap, and the boxer's torso, which gave the original its impact, is lost.

The lockup is shrunk to about 60% of the width, and the small x-row and the FOR box are near illegible at this size. The weakest: the lockup is the smallest of the three (about 45% of the width), so the FOR box text and the row of x-marks are tiny and weak against the busy dark photo. The headline and body are readable at the top, but the brush stroke floats above them, disconnected. The brick photo is shrunk to a narrow strip in the middle, and a large empty band sits below it. The best restructure: the brick photo sits on top, then a strong headline, then readable body copy. It has the same flaws as candidate 3, slightly better balanced: a detached brush stroke at the top and a small brick strip floating in the middle. The empty gaps around the brick photo are uneven. Looks identical to candidate 3: tiny low-contrast quote over a busy area of the photo, attribution split off and crowded against the right edge, an unbalanced empty middle, and a crop that loses the child.

Better left-to-right arrangement than the others: quote on the left, attribution pushed to the right. But the quote type is about 7 px and barely legible over a busy, light part of the photo. Quote and attribution are shrunk to a tiny centred column that cannot be read at this size, with low contrast over the busy hand and face area. The rest of the banner is empty dark photo, and nothing has been rearranged to read left to right. Unusable.

Same structure as candidate 1 with a slightly taller image block. The date/address is still isolated on the far right, away from the headline, the image is centred instead of edge-bleeding, and the right third is mostly empty. The layout is fragmented.

The best of the four: it reads left to right with a legible windmill and a clear headline on the right. The same as candidate 1: the windmill is a tiny icon crushed at the bottom edge under the headline, and the red and blue shapes are clipped slivers. The oversized green shape on the left pulls the eye, and the right side is empty, so the layout is lopsided.

A shrunk copy of the square original pasted into the centre. The headline and windmill are microscopic and unreadable, about 90% of the banner is empty white, and nothing was rearranged for the wide format.

Turned into a proper left-to-right banner with a dominant one-line headline, but the yellow block sits awkwardly over the cramped left photo crop, the second photo is cut down to a sliver behind its frame, and the two black label chips on the right are split by an uneven gap with too little margin from the edge.

Nearly the same layout as candidate 1, but the left photo crop is muddier, with the yellow bars cutting across the subject's face and arm, and the narrow right photo strip is just as weak. The label chips are still loosely grouped at the far right.

Shrunk copy of the original placed in the middle of the banner: all text except 'Grand Opening' is unreadably tiny (address, date, URL, SHOWROOM), and about 60% of the canvas is empty white on both sides. No real re-layout.

Strong single-line 'PLAYFUL LEARNING' headline, but the kicker is moved below it and shrunk to illegible micro-text, which breaks the reading order; the photo is a postage-stamp thumbnail lost among the decorative squares in a cluttered right corner.

Nearly identical to candidate 1: divider rule collides with 'WANT', the oversized empty chevron panel competes with the headline, dot grid is cropped at the canvas edge; only slightly more breathing room above and below the panels.

Just a shrunk copy of the portrait layout dropped in the middle: headline and sub-copy are unreadably tiny, the chevron bar is a sliver, and about 90% of the banner is dead photo. It does not fit the format at all.

Effectively the same as candidate 3. The original's look survives, but the layout was not adapted to the square: the headline is small, the content is a narrow centred column, and the left and right thirds are dead space. Ranked just below 3 only because the two are tied.

Faithful and intact: the headline, the small chevron and the nurse bleeding off the bottom all keep the original's order and proportions. But it is just the portrait layout scaled down and centred. A shrunk copy of the original placed in the middle of the tall canvas. The headline is microscopic and unreadable, and about 80% of the canvas is empty white. It makes no attempt to fit the vertical format.
